slot.brief: Combustion analysis of a hydrocarbon + oxygen mixture with volume contraction data (CO2 and H2O measured); find the mole fraction of fuel in the original mixture — multi-step stoichiometry.

stem: An acyclic alkane–oxygen mixture is completely burnt. At a common reference temperature and pressure, it forms $48$ mL of $\text{CO}_2$ and water equivalent to $72$ mL of vapour. The cooled, dry products occupy $120$ mL; the initial mixture volume exceeds this by $60$ mL. What was the alkane mole fraction initially?

verdicts.working: Let the alkane be CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with volume x. Product volumes give nx = 48 and (n+1)x = 72, so x = 24 mL and n = 2. Initial mixture volume = 120 + 60 = 180 mL, hence the alkane mole fraction is 24/180 = 2/15.

working:
For $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$, $\dfrac{V_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}}{V_{\text{CO}_2}}=\dfrac{n+1}{n}=\dfrac{72}{48}=\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $n=2$.
$V_{\text{alkane}}=\dfrac{48}{2}=24$ mL.
$V_{\text{initial}}=120+60=180$ mL.
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6+\dfrac{7}{2}\text{O}_2\rightarrow2\text{CO}_2+3\text{H}_2\text{O}$; the initial oxygen is $156$ mL and the excess is $72$ mL, giving $48+72=120$ mL dry products.
$x_{\text{alkane}}=\dfrac{24}{180}=\dfrac{2}{15}$. Independent check: Let the alkane be CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with volume x. Product volumes give nx = 48 and (n+1)x = 72, so x = 24 mL and n = 2. Initial mixture volume = 120 + 60 = 180 mL, hence the alkane mole fraction is 24/180 = 2/15.
solution:
For $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$, $\frac{V_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}}{V_{\text{CO}_2}}=\frac{n+1}{n}=\frac{72}{48}=\frac{3}{2}$, giving $n=2$ and alkane volume $48/2=24$ mL.
The initial mixture volume is $120+60=180$ mL, so the alkane mole fraction is
$$x=\frac{24}{180}=\frac{2}{15}.$$
